summary: Defines a protocol for carrying ISDN Q.921 user messages over IP using SCTP, between a signaling gateway and a media gateway controller. The gateway receives ISDN signaling on a standard ISDN interface and passes it on. It replaces RFC 3057 and is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: An ISDN line carries its call setup messages on a separate channel from the speech. This document defines how to move those setup messages off the telephone line and across an IP network, so that the software deciding what to do with each call can run somewhere else. The signalling gateway receives the messages on the line and passes them on; the media gateway controller does the processing.

questions: what is an application server process
how does isdn failover between controllers work
subtitle: Carrying the signalling of an ISDN telephone line across an IP network to a media gateway controller.

tldr.problem: ISDN signalling stops at the edge of a telephone network. A carrier that wants to process calls in a central data centre needs to carry that signalling across the IP network to the machines doing the processing.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines the Q.921-User Adaptation Layer, a protocol that runs over SCTP between a signalling gateway and a media gateway controller, and that carries the ISDN boundary primitives and the call setup messages themselves.
tldr.outcome: This obsoletes RFC 3057 and is itself an IETF-defined SIGTRAN adaptation layer. It also defines how a standby media gateway controller takes over when the active one fails.

facts.label: SCTP and TCP user port number for IUA

today: RFC 4233 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted, so it remains the current Q.921-User Adaptation Layer specification. It replaced RFC 3057, and it was later updated by RFC 5133.

sections.title: The Backhaul Problem
sections.content:
In this document, the term Q.921-User refers to an upper layer that uses the services of Q.921, not the user side of the ISDN interface. Examples of the upper layer would be Q.931 and QSIG.

There is a need for Switched Circuit Network signalling protocol delivery from an ISDN Signaling Gateway to a Media Gateway Controller as described in the Framework Architecture for Signaling Transport. The delivery mechanism should meet three criteria: support for transport of the Q.921/Q.931 boundary primitives, support for communication between Layer Management modules on the gateway and the controller, and support for management of SCTP active associations between the gateway and the controller.

The document supports both ISDN Primary Rate Access as well as Basic Rate Access, including the support for both point-to-point and point-to-multipoint modes of communication. This support includes Facility Associated Signaling, Non-Facility Associated Signaling, and NFAS with backup D channel. QSIG adaptation layer requirements do not differ from Q.931 adaptation layer, so the procedures described here also apply to a QSIG adaptation layer. For simplicity, only Q.931 is mentioned in the rest of the document.
sections.plainLanguage: A telephone company's local exchange knows a lot about the calls on its lines, but it cannot do much with them. To put call processing in a data centre, the setup messages have to travel over IP. This document is the protocol that carries them.

sections.title: The Roles and Their Names
sections.content:
An Application Server is a logical entity serving a specific application instance. An example is a media gateway controller handling the Q.931 and call processing for D channels terminated by the signaling gateways. In practice an Application Server is modelled at the gateway as an ordered list of one or more related Application Server Processes, for example primary, secondary and tertiary.

An Application Server Process is a process instance of an Application Server, for example primary or backup media gateway controller instances. A host is the computing platform that the process is running on. Backhaul means that a gateway terminates the lower layers of an SCN protocol and backhauls the upper layers to the controller for call processing; here the gateway terminates Q.921 and backhauls Q.931.

An association refers to an SCTP association, which provides the transport for the delivery of Q.921-User protocol data units and IUA adaptation layer peer messages. A stream refers to an SCTP stream, a uni-directional logical channel established from one SCTP endpoint to another, within which all user messages are delivered in sequence except for those submitted to the un-ordered delivery service.

The Interface Identifier identifies the physical interface at the gateway for which the signaling messages are sent or received. Its format can be text or integer, and the values are assigned by network operator policy, of local significance only and coordinated between the gateway and the application server process; significance is not implied across gateways served by an application server.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three names to keep apart. The gateway is the box at the edge of the telephone network. The controller is the program that does the work. The application server is the logical service, which may have several controller processes behind it, and the interface identifier says which line a message came in on.

sections.title: The Gateway and the Controller
sections.content:
The architecture defined for SCN signaling transport over IP uses multiple components: an IP transport protocol, a signaling common transport protocol, and an adaptation module to support the services expected by a particular SCN signaling protocol from its underlying protocol layer. This document defines an adaptation module suitable for the transport of ISDN Q.921-User messages.

In a Signaling Gateway, the ISDN signaling is expected to be received over a standard ISDN network termination. The gateway then provides interworking of transport functions with IP Signaling Transport, in order to transport the Q.931 signaling messages to the media gateway controller where the peer Q.931 protocol layer exists.

It is recommended that the IUA use the services of SCTP as the underlying reliable common signaling transport protocol. The use of SCTP provides explicit packet-oriented delivery rather than stream-oriented delivery, sequenced delivery of user messages within multiple streams with an option for order-of-arrival delivery, optional multiplexing of user messages into SCTP datagrams, network-level fault tolerance through support of multi-homing at either or both ends of an association, resistance to flooding and masquerade attacks, and data segmentation to conform to the discovered path MTU size.

There are scenarios without redundancy requirements, and scenarios in which redundancy is supported below the transport layer. In these cases the SCTP functions above MAY be determined to not be required and TCP MAY be used as the underlying common transport protocol. The SCTP and TCP registered user port number assignment for IUA is 9900. The default orientation would be for the gateway to take on the role of server while the application server process is the client, so that processes initiate the SCTP association to the gateway.
sections.plainLanguage: The protocol stack from the top down is: the call setup protocol, the ISDN data link layer, this adaptation layer, SCTP, and IP. SCTP is preferred because it keeps messages in order per stream and can survive a broken path, but plain TCP is allowed where redundancy is already handled lower down.

sections.title: The Primitives the IUA Layer Provides
sections.content:
Three groups of services are defined.

First, support for transport of Q.921/Q.931 boundary primitives. The IUA layer needs to support all the primitives of this boundary to successfully backhaul Q.931. The DL-ESTABLISH primitives are used to request, indicate and confirm the outcome of the procedures for establishing multiple frame operation. The DL-RELEASE primitives are used to request, indicate and confirm the outcome of the procedures for terminating a previously established multiple frame operation, or for reporting an unsuccessful establishment attempt. The DL-DATA primitives are used to request and indicate layer 3 Q.931 messages that are to be transmitted or received using the acknowledged information transfer service, and the DL-UNIT DATA primitives do the same for the unacknowledged information transfer service.

Second, support for communication between Layer Management modules on the gateway and the controller. The M-TEI STATUS primitives are used to request, confirm and indicate the status, assigned or unassigned, of an ISDN Terminal Endpoint Identifier. The M-ERROR primitive is used to indicate an error with a received IUA message, for example an interface identifier value that is not known to the gateway.

Third, support for management of active associations. The M-SCTP ESTABLISH and M-SCTP RELEASE primitives request, indicate and confirm the establishment and release of an SCTP association to a peer IUA node, and the M-SCTP STATUS primitive reports the status of the underlying association. The M-ASP STATUS, M-ASP-UP, M-ASP-DOWN, M-ASP-ACTIVE, M-ASP-INACTIVE and M-AS STATUS primitives let Layer Management read and change the state of an application server process and of an application server, so that messages can be exchanged between IUA peers to stop traffic to a local IUA user.
sections.plainLanguage: Two kinds of instruction travel over this link. Some carry the telephone conversation's setup messages themselves. Others are the local management talking to the protocol, asking it to open a connection, report whether it is up, or stop sending traffic to a particular controller.

sections.title: The Common Message Header
sections.content:
The protocol messages for Q.921-User Adaptation require a message header that contains the adaptation layer version, the message type and the message length. All fields in an IUA message MUST be transmitted in the network byte order, unless otherwise stated. The version field contains the version of the IUA adaptation layer; the supported version is 1, Release 1.0.

The Message Class field is 8 bits. Class 0 is for management messages, class 1 and 2 are reserved for other SIGTRAN adaptation layers, class 3 is for ASP State Maintenance messages, class 4 is for ASP Traffic Maintenance messages, class 5 is for Q.921/Q.931 Boundary Primitives Transport messages, classes 6 to 8 are reserved for other SIGTRAN adaptation layers, classes 9 to 127 are reserved by the IETF, and classes 128 to 255 are reserved for IETF-defined message class extensions.

Within the QPTM class, the message types are 1 Data Request, 2 Data Indication, 3 Unit Data Request, 4 Unit Data Indication, 5 Establish Request, 6 Establish Confirm, 7 Establish Indication, 8 Release Request, 9 Release Confirm and 10 Release Indication. Within the ASP State Maintenance class, the types are 1 ASP Up, 2 ASP Down, 3 Heartbeat, 4 ASP Up Ack, 5 ASP Down Ack and 6 Heartbeat Ack. When an implementation receives a message type that it does not support, it MUST respond with an Error message with an Error Code of Unsupported Message Type.
sections.plainLanguage: Every message starts with the same eight bytes: which version of the protocol, which family of message, which message within that family, and how long the whole thing is. The family tells you at a glance whether you are looking at call setup traffic or at housekeeping about which controller is in charge.

sections.title: The IUA Message Header
sections.content:
In addition to the common message header, there is a specific message header for the QPTM and the TEI Status management messages. The IUA message header immediately follows the common header in these messages. It contains the Interface Identifier and the Data Link Connection Identifier.

The Interface Identifier identifies the physical interface terminating the signaling channel at the gateway for which the signaling messages are sent or received. Its format can be text or integer, and the integer-formatted Interface Identifier MUST be supported while the text-formatted one MAY optionally be supported. The integer form is carried in a parameter with tag 0x1 and a length always set to 8; the text form is carried in a parameter with tag 0x3 and a variable length.

The DLCI is carried in a parameter with tag 0x5 and a length of 8, and holds the Service Access Point Identifier in 6 bits, the Terminal Endpoint Identifier in 7 bits, and a spare bit. The DLCI field is coded in accordance with Q.921. As an example, a Service Access Point Identifier of 0, a Terminal Endpoint Identifier of 64 and a spare value of 0 are encoded as 0x0, 0x81 and 0x0.
sections.plainLanguage: The second header says which line the message belongs to and which logical connection on it. The interface identifier names the physical line, and the DLCI names the terminal and service point on that line, using the same encoding the telephone network itself uses.

sections.title: The States of a Controller Process
sections.content:
The IUA layer on the gateway maintains the state of each application server process as well as the state of the application server. The state of a process changes because of the reception of messages from the peer IUA layer at that process, the reception of some messages from the peer IUA layer at other processes in the application server, the reception of indications from the SCTP layer, or local management intervention.

There are three states. ASP-DOWN means the process is unavailable and the related SCTP association is down; initially all processes are in this state, and a process in this state SHOULD NOT be sent any IUA messages. ASP-INACTIVE means the remote IUA peer is available and the association is up but application traffic is stopped; in this state the process can be sent any non-QPTM IUA messages except TEI Status messages. ASP-ACTIVE means the remote peer is available and application traffic is active.

Between the states, an ASP Up or ASP Inactive moves a process into the inactive state, an ASP Active moves it into the active state, and an ASP Down or an SCTP failure moves it back down. An alternate process taking over is shown as a move into the active state.
sections.plainLanguage: Each controller process is in one of three conditions: down, up but idle, or up and taking calls. When the active one fails, a standby one is told to become active, and the gateway starts sending it the traffic instead.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
The security considerations discussed in Security Considerations for Signaling Transport protocols apply to this document.

The use of SCTP also brings its own properties: resistance to flooding and masquerade attacks, and network-level fault tolerance through support of multi-homing at either or both ends of an association. The document also notes that if the IUA layer becomes congested, it MAY stop reading from the SCTP association to flow control from the peer IUA.
sections.plainLanguage: The security analysis of the signalling transport framework applies here unchanged. SCTP adds some protection of its own against flooding and impersonation, and the protocol can also push back on a peer that is sending too fast.

fields.desc: The version of the IUA adaptation layer. The supported version is 1, Release 1.0.

fields.desc: 0 for management, 3 for ASP state maintenance, 4 for ASP traffic maintenance, 5 for boundary primitives transport.

fields.desc: The type of message within its class.

items.label: Management
items.desc: MGMT messages between the IUA layer and local management.

items.label: ASP State Maintenance
items.desc: ASPSM messages, such as ASP Up, ASP Down and Heartbeat.

items.label: ASP Traffic Maintenance
items.desc: ASPTM messages, such as ASP Active and ASP Inactive.

items.label: Boundary Primitives Transport
items.desc: QPTM messages that carry the Q.921/Q.931 boundary primitives.

viz.caption: THE PRIMITIVES THE ADAPTATION LAYER OFFERS

items.title: DL-ESTABLISH
items.text: Requests, indicates and confirms the establishment of multiple frame operation on the signaling channel.

items.title: DL-RELEASE
items.text: Requests, indicates and confirms the termination of that operation, or reports an unsuccessful attempt.

items.title: DL-DATA
items.text: Carries layer 3 Q.931 messages using the acknowledged information transfer service.

items.title: DL-UNIT DATA
items.text: Carries layer 3 Q.931 messages using the unacknowledged information transfer service.

items.title: M-SCTP ESTABLISH and STATUS
items.text: Let local management establish, release and monitor the SCTP associations between the gateway and the controller.

items.title: M-ASP STATUS, UP, DOWN, ACTIVE, INACTIVE
items.text: Let local management read and change the state of an application server process.
